bib.title: Are Long-LLMs A Necessity For Long-Context Tasks?

question: Can long-context tasks be solved with a short-context LLM by strategically accessing and using parts of the input, instead of a long-context LLM?
hypothesis: Most long-context tasks are short-context solvable: they can be solved from oracle short contexts within the input.
contributions: Identify the problem of solving long-context tasks with short-LLMs
Propose LC-Boost, which adaptively reasons about how to access and utilize long context
Empirically verify effectiveness with superior performance at low resource consumption

method.summary: LC-Boost splits a long input into chunks and has a short-context LLM (GPT-3.5-turbo-16K, limited to 4K working context) pick a processing strategy via a [Task Understanding] prompt, then run a loop of discrete actions (Retrieve, Move, Append, Merge, Answer, Aggregation) over chunks, accumulating extracted evidence, then answer. Compared with short, long and closed-source LLMs on 12 datasets, mostly LongBench.
method.task: long-context QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic counting, code completion

datasets.name: LongBench subsets (NarrativeQA, Qasper, MultiFieldQA, HotpotQA, 2WikiMQA, MuSiQue, GovReport, MultiNews, SAMSum, PassageCount, LCC)
datasets.size: 200 samples each except MultiFieldQA 150 and LCC 500; avg length 1,235 (LCC) to 18,409 (Narrative)
datasets.preprocessing: context truncated from the middle when exceeding a model's limit (following LongBench)

datasets.name: Self-constructed dataset
datasets.size: 32 queries over 6 sources (ACL 2023 paper list 44,490, Diamond Sutra 19,993, 2024 Olympics schedule 15,844, Big Bang Theory S3E14 subtitle 11,136, The Little Prince 22,471, Harry Potter 2 122,591); avg length 39,420

other.note: foundation model of LC-Boost; also baseline

inference.prompting: Prompt-only LC-Boost: [Task Understanding] prompt with few-shot examples chooses option 1-4; chunk prompts [Append] (select up to ten key sentences by id), [Merge] (supplement previous summary), LongBench task prompt with 'null' instruction for scan. Final answer uses LongBench prompt with surrogate context.
inference.retrieval: BGE-Reranker-Large ranks all chunks (option 1); top-k not stated. Chunk size not stated beyond 4K working context. Code completion browses context in reverse (near to far).

other.energy_practice: Llama2-7B-128K (brute-force) vs Llama2-7B-chat-4K (LC-Boost), GPU time and power recorded

metrics.name: Token consumption
metrics.definition: end-to-end tokens relative to brute force

baselines: ablation action-space variants incl. Retrieve only, Merge only, Append only, Random, Brute-force
eval.protocol: Baselines run with LongBench settings; single numbers, no seeds or significance tests reported.

prompts.text:
You need to process a task with a long context that greatly exceeds your context limit.
The only feasible way to handle this is by processing the long context chunk by chunk.
Below is the original task prompt:
{task_prompt}
Below is the query:
{input_query}
You have the following options to process the long context. Choose one of them:
[1]. Retrieve the chunk most relevant to the input query to support answer generation.
[2]. Summarize each chunk and then aggregate the summaries after processing all chunks.
[3]. Extract key sentences from each chunk and then aggregate them after processing all chunks.
[4]. Sequentially scan chunks and produce the answer as soon as the query can be answered.
Below are some examples for reference:
The examples begin as follows:
{examples}
The examples conclude here.
Please learn the examples and select one of the options by only outputting the corresponding index number.

You are given an article and a question. Read the article carefully and follow my instructions to process it.
Article:
The article begins as follows:
{article}
The article concludes here.
Question:
{question}
Instructions:
Each sentence in the article is marked with a sentence identifier [si], for example [s1].
Select up to ten key sentences from the article that are most likely to answer the question.
Only output the selected sentence identifiers, separated by commas.
Example: [s39],[s54]
If no sentences are relevant, please output "null".

You are provided with a portion of an article, a question, and summarization of the article's previous portions. Read the article portion and follow my instructions to process it.
...
Instruction:
Summarize the partial article to supplement the previous summarization, which can better support the task.
If no content needs to be supplemented, please output "null".

evidence.quote: we employ GPT-3.5 as the foundation model for LC-Boost in the subsequent experiments

results.claim: LC-Boost with a 4K context beats all baselines on multi-doc QA, 56.4 vs next best 49.1 (DeepSeek-v2).
results.setup: 12 datasets, GPT-3.5-turbo-16K as LC-Boost base, 4K context

results.claim: LC-Boost improves single-doc QA over its own base model GPT-3.5-turbo-16K.
LC-Boost on the synthetic tasks vs GPT-3.5-turbo-16K.
LC-Boost does not win code completion; Yi-9B-200K scores higher.
results.note: Table 3 prints Yi-9B-200K LCC as 72.0, Table 1 as 72.1

results.claim: Summarization gain over GPT-3.5-turbo-16K is small.
On the self-constructed whole-context reasoning set LC-Boost scores 47.7 vs GPT-3.5-turbo-16K 32.9.
Token consumption of LC-Boost on NarrativeQA is a third of brute force; on GovReport it is higher.
results.quote: LC-Boost’s token consumption was 34.1% of the brute-force method’s consumption in NarrativeQA, 112% in GovReport, and 29.5% in LCC

results.claim: Pilot study: LC-Boost with 4K context performs as well as or better than GPT-4-128K brute force on all task groups (bar heights not given in text).
results.setup: GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 as base, LongBench task groups

results.claim: Dynamic action selection beats fixed strategies in ablation, especially for single and multi-doc QA, but not for few-shot SAMSum (values only in Fig 3).
Long LLMs are inconsistent across tasks, e.g. Yi-9B-200K scores 14.6 on few-shot but 72.1 on code; authors infer long-context adaptation may harm general ability.
Case: counting single-author ACL 2023 papers (45K context), LC-Boost answers 8 (correct) while Phi-3-mini-128K says 11, GPT-3.5-turbo-16K 0, Claude-3-Haiku 1.
Brute-force energy grows markedly with context length, LC-Boost at 4K grows only mildly; no numeric values in text.

limits: Authors concede some tasks may need the full context and LC-Boost may fail there.
Discrete action space; free-form action prediction was unstable with GPT-3.5.
Only GPT-3.5 used as base model; open-source LLMs lacked zero-shot instruction following.
Token cost can exceed brute force for aggregation tasks (112% on GovReport).
No seeds, variance or significance tests; chunk size, top-k and decoding settings not stated; no code release stated.
Theory (DPI) is argued with conditions (independent chunks, optimal compression) that rarely hold; the pilot study reports bar charts without numbers in text.
Energy comparison compares different models (7B-128K vs 7B-4K) and includes multi-GPU effects.

terms.definition: long-context tasks can be solved by purely working with oracle short-contexts within the long-context tasks' inputs
